name: TC Televisión Armed Takeover
detail: Gunmen storm the TC Televisión studio in Guayaquil in apparent retaliation for the government crackdown that followed Fito's escape, taking staff hostage live on air.

name: Assassination of Prosecutor César Suárez
detail: Suárez, who was leading the investigation into the TC Televisión attack, is shot dead in Guayaquil in an apparent gang reprisal.

name: Esmeraldas Double Car Bombing
detail: Two car bombs detonate simultaneously in Esmeraldas, one outside a school, in an apparent show of force by trafficking groups contesting the province's states of emergency.

name: Litoral Penitentiary Gang-on-Gang Riot
detail: The 'Duendes' gang attacks rival 'Freddy Kruegers' inmates at Litoral Penitentiary, killing 15-17, followed by at least 12 retaliatory killings in the Portete neighborhood in the following days.

name: Machala Prison Riot
detail: Fourteen inmates killed in gang-on-gang fighting at a Machala prison, part of a wave of retaliatory prison violence tied to the Choneros-Lobos rivalry.

name: Esmeraldas Prison Riot
detail: Los Choneros- and Los Lobos-aligned inmates clash at an Esmeraldas prison days after the Machala riot, killing at least 17, two by decapitation, in an escalating cycle of prison retaliation.

name: Guayaquil Shopping Mall Car Bombing
detail: A vehicle-borne explosive device kills one person outside a Guayaquil mall; a second device is found and defused nearby, in an apparent intimidation campaign against the government's security operations.

name: Manabí Bridge Bombings
detail: A local criminal gang, allegedly working with Colombian ex-FARC dissidents, bombs two bridges in apparent retaliation for a major military crackdown on illegal mining operations linked to the groups.

name: Plot Against Interior Minister Reimberg
detail: Los Tiguerones leadership, through alias 'Gato Negro,' allegedly plans an attack against Interior Minister John Reimberg in apparent retaliation for his role directing security operations against the gang.

name: Murder of Journalist Patricio Aguilar
detail: Community journalist Patricio Aguilar is murdered in Quinindé after receiving threats tied to his reporting on local gang activity, in an apparent act of intimidation against independent press coverage of trafficking networks.
